messages.content:
FRAMEFLOW — Build a Complete Creative Operating System

1. Product Vision

Build a premium, modern, fully functional web application called FrameFlow.

Tagline: Every idea deserves to become a story.

FrameFlow is an all-in-one personal Creative Operating System designed for photographers, filmmakers, documentary creators, screenwriters, visual storytellers and creative individuals.

It should bring the entire creative journey into one workspace — from capturing a random idea to researching, writing, planning, shooting, editing and archiving a finished creative project.

This is NOT a generic task management application, notes app or simple portfolio website.

It should feel like a combination of:

* Notion’s organisational capabilities.
* Final Cut Pro’s cinematic creative atmosphere.
* Pinterest’s visual inspiration experience.
* A professional screenplay writing application.
* A photographer’s personal archive.

The experience must be immersive, elegant, organised and genuinely useful.

2. Design Philosophy

Create a sophisticated cinematic dark interface.

Visual identity

* Background: Deep charcoal / near-black.
* Primary text: Warm off-white.
* Accent: Muted amber or warm beige.
* Secondary text: Soft grey.
* Borders: Subtle dark grey.
* Cards: Slightly elevated charcoal surfaces.
* Use elegant editorial typography.
* Use generous whitespace.
* Use high-quality photography and cinematic imagery.

UI principles

* Minimal and distraction-free.
* Premium, editorial aesthetic.
* Smooth transitions and subtle animations.
* Beautiful hover and focus interactions.
* Responsive layouts for iPad, desktop and mobile.
* Touch-friendly navigation and controls.
* Consistent spacing, typography and iconography.

Avoid:

* Generic admin dashboard designs.
* Excessive gradients.
* Bright neon colours.
* Unnecessary glassmorphism.
* Overcrowded screens.
* Excessive rounded cards.
* Placeholder buttons that do nothing.

3. Application Structure

Create the following primary navigation:

1. Home
2. My Projects
3. Photography Studio
4. Scriptwriting Studio
5. Documentary Studio
6. Film Production
7. Inspiration Vault
8. Creative Journal
9. Archive
10. Settings

The navigation should be collapsible on desktop and adapted for tablet and mobile.

4. Home Dashboard

Build a personalised creative dashboard.

Include:

Welcome section

* Greeting based on the time of day.
* A short creative quote.
* Quick-create buttons.

Continue Creating

Display recently accessed projects with:

* Cover image.
* Project title.
* Project category.
* Last updated date.
* Progress indicator.

Creative Overview

Show:

* Total active projects.
* Photographs archived.
* Scripts in progress.
* Documentaries in development.
* Ideas captured.

Recent Activity

Display recent creative activities.

Quick Actions

* New Photography Project.
* New Film.
* New Documentary.
* New Script.
* Capture an Idea.
* Create a Moodboard.

5. My Projects — Central Project Management

This is the heart of FrameFlow.

Every creative activity should be organised into projects.

Allow users to create projects with:

* Project name.
* Project description.
* Project category.
* Cover image.
* Start date.
* Target completion date.
* Status.
* Tags.

Project categories:

* Photography.
* Short Film.
* Feature Film.
* Documentary.
* Screenplay.
* Travel Story.
* Personal Creative Project.
* Other.

Each project must have its own dedicated workspace.

Inside each project, provide:

* Overview.
* Notes.
* Documents.
* Images and references.
* Tasks and milestones.
* Timeline.
* Files.
* Activity history.

Allow users to add, edit, delete, archive and search projects.

6. Photography Studio

Build a complete photography management workspace.

Photography Library

* Upload photographs.
* Create albums and collections.
* Add descriptions and captions.
* Add tags and categories.
* Search and filter photographs.
* View photographs in grid and masonry layouts.
* Open photographs in a full-screen viewer.

Shoot Planner

Allow users to plan photography sessions.

Fields:

* Shoot title.
* Location.
* Date.
* Shoot concept.
* Lighting conditions.
* Camera and lens.
* Shot list.
* Reference images.
* Notes.

Equipment Library

Allow users to maintain a personal gear collection:

* Camera bodies.
* Lenses.
* Accessories.
* Filters.
* Lighting equipment.

Photography Challenges

Support challenges such as 100 Days, 100 Photographs.

Include:

* Daily submission.
* Completion tracking.
* Calendar view.
* Photograph gallery.
* Challenge progress.

Portfolio

Create a beautiful public-facing photography portfolio layout with selected photographs, categories and project descriptions.

7. Scriptwriting Studio

Build a professional screenplay and creative writing environment.

Writing Editor

Provide a clean, distraction-free writing interface.

Support:

* Screenplay formatting.
* Scene headings.
* Action descriptions.
* Character names.
* Dialogue.
* Parentheticals.
* Transitions.
* Standard text and headings.

Include keyboard-friendly formatting controls.

Script Management

* Create multiple scripts.
* Save drafts automatically.
* Track versions.
* Organise scripts by project.
* Export scripts as PDF.
* Search scripts.

Story Development

Create dedicated sections for:

* Logline.
* Synopsis.
* Story concept.
* Three-act structure.
* Character development.
* Plot points.
* Themes.
* Ending.

Character Library

Each character should have:

* Name.
* Age.
* Appearance.
* Personality.
* Background.
* Motivation.
* Character arc.
* Reference images.

Scene Breakdown

Each scene should contain:

* Scene number.
* Location.
* Interior / Exterior.
* Day / Night.
* Characters.
* Scene description.
* Dialogue.
* Production notes.

8. Documentary Studio

Create a dedicated documentary development environment.

Features:

Documentary Research

* Research notes.
* Sources and reference links.
* Important facts.
* Historical context.
* Subject profiles.
* Research attachments.

Interview Planner

* Interviewee details.
* Interview questions.
* Recording notes.
* Interview status.
* Key quotes.
* Follow-up questions.

Narrative Development

* Documentary concept.
* Central question.
* Narrative structure.
* Chapters or sequences.
* Story progression.
* Supporting evidence.

Documentary Timeline

Organise research, interviews, footage and milestones chronologically.

9. Film Production Studio

Build a pre-production planning environment.

Storyboard

* Create storyboard scenes.
* Upload reference images.
* Add scene descriptions.
* Add camera angle and movement.
* Organise frames sequentially.

Shot List

Include:

* Shot number.
* Scene.
* Shot type.
* Camera angle.
* Camera movement.
* Lens.
* Lighting.
* Description.
* Production status.

Location Library

* Location name.
* Address.
* Photographs.
* Lighting references.
* Scouting notes.
* Shooting requirements.

Production Planner

* Shooting schedule.
* Cast details.
* Crew details.
* Equipment checklist.
* Production tasks.
* Completion status.

10. Inspiration Vault

Create a visual-first creative inspiration library.

Allow users to save:

* Photographs.
* Images.
* Film references.
* Website links.
* Articles.
* Quotes.
* Videos.
* Creative concepts.
* Moodboards.

Features:

* Create custom collections.
* Add tags.
* Add descriptions.
* Search and filter.
* Link references to projects.
* Build visual moodboards using drag-and-drop functionality.

The interface should feel like a private Pinterest for creative professionals.

11. Creative Journal

Create a personal creative diary.

Features:

* Daily journal entries.
* Quick idea capture.
* Observations.
* Travel experiences.
* Creative thoughts.
* Writing prompts.
* Personal milestones.

Include a calendar-based journal view and searchable entries.

12. AI Creative Assistant

Integrate an AI assistant throughout the application.

The assistant should help with:

Photography

* Generate photography concepts.
* Suggest compositions.
* Create shot ideas.
* Suggest lighting approaches.
* Develop photoshoot concepts.

Screenwriting

* Improve dialogue.
* Develop characters.
* Identify plot inconsistencies.
* Suggest scene ideas.
* Improve story structure.

Documentary

* Generate research questions.
* Suggest interview questions.
* Organise research.
* Develop documentary narratives.

Film Production

* Generate shot lists from scene descriptions.
* Suggest camera movements.
* Create production checklists.
* Convert scripts into scene breakdowns.

General Creativity

* Expand rough ideas.
* Generate creative prompts.
* Connect related ideas.
* Help overcome creative blocks.

The AI must never automatically overwrite original user content. Always preserve the original and let users accept or reject suggestions.

Keep AI integration modular so API credentials can be configured securely later.

13. Archive

Create a permanent archive for completed projects.

Include:

* Completed films.
* Published documentaries.
* Finished photography collections.
* Final scripts.
* Personal milestones.

Allow users to revisit and restore archived projects.

14. Technology Stack

Use the following technology stack:

Frontend:

* Next.js.
* React.
* TypeScript.
* Tailwind CSS.
* shadcn/ui.
* Lucide icons.

Backend:

* Supabase.
* PostgreSQL.
* Supabase Authentication.
* Supabase Storage.

AI:

* OpenAI API integration, designed to be configurable through secure environment variables.

Additional:

* Recharts for analytics.
* A reliable rich-text editor.
* Drag-and-drop support.
* PDF export functionality.

15. Database Architecture

Design a scalable relational database.

Create appropriate tables for:

* Users.
* Projects.
* Project files.
* Project notes.
* Tasks.
* Milestones.
* Photographs.
* Albums.
* Photography equipment.
* Scripts.
* Script versions.
* Characters.
* Scenes.
* Documentaries.
* Research notes.
* Interviews.
* Storyboards.
* Shot lists.
* Locations.
* Moodboards.
* Inspiration references.
* Journal entries.
* AI conversations.

Use proper relationships, foreign keys, timestamps and Row Level Security.

Users must only access their own private data.

16. Functional Requirements

This must be a functional application, not merely a visual prototype.

Implement:

* Authentication.
* Project creation and management.
* CRUD operations.
* File uploads.
* Image previews.
* Search and filtering.
* Persistent data storage.
* Autosaving.
* Responsive navigation.
* Functional forms.
* Working modals and menus.
* Empty states.
* Error states.
* Loading states.

Do not use fake buttons or decorative controls.

Use realistic demo data only where necessary and clearly distinguish it from actual user content.

17. Development Approach

Build the application in phases.

Phase 1:

* Establish the design system.
* Create the application shell.
* Build the navigation.
* Implement the home dashboard.
* Implement project management.

Phase 2:

* Photography Studio.
* Scriptwriting Studio.
* Creative Journal.

Phase 3:

* Documentary Studio.
* Film Production Studio.
* Inspiration Vault.

Phase 4:

* Supabase integration.
* Authentication.
* Persistent file storage.
* Database relationships.

Phase 5:

* AI Creative Assistant.
* Advanced interactions.
* Export functionality.
* Performance optimisation.

18. Important Final Instructions

Before writing code:

1. Understand the entire product vision.
2. Plan the architecture.
3. Establish reusable components.
4. Design the database schema.
5. Define the navigation and user flows.

Do not attempt to build every feature in one rushed implementation.

Start by creating a polished, working foundation and then progressively implement every module.

Prioritise excellent UX, beautiful visual design, maintainable code and real functionality.

The final result should feel like a premium creative software product — a digital home for someone who loves photography, cinema, storytelling, documentaries and writing.

FrameFlow is not just an app to organise creative work. It is a place where an individual’s entire creative journey lives.
